response: Observed fact: motor temperature reading is 96 C. That does not identify the hidden cause.
Live causes: real overload, cooling failure, drifting sensor, transient spike.
Discriminators: compare motor current/load, read a second independent temperature sensor, inspect airflow/cooling state, and check whether the reading persists over time.

Belief update rule: high current plus corroborating temperature raises overload; normal current plus poor airflow raises cooling failure; disagreement with a second sensor raises sensor-fault probability; rapid normalization without corroboration raises transient-spike probability.
Classify the write outcome as unknown, not failed.
Read the target path and predecessor/current state before any retry.

If the intended content already exists, record success and do not retry. If absent, retry only with an exact expected predecessor/currentness guard. If conflicting content exists, stop and reconcile rather than overwrite.
Preserve the original conclusion's exact commit/blob bindings as historical evidence.
Fetch the branch's current head before making a current claim and inspect whether the relevant contract/source changed.
Record current compatibility or incompatibility as a new fact; do not rewrite the old provenance to the new head.
Treat the five agent outputs as one correlated evidence family because they share the same source and prompt dependency.
Evaluate the independent dataset separately by evidence quality, design, and relevance rather than by vote count.
Trace the conflict to source assumptions or measurement differences. If it cannot be resolved, preserve the disagreement instead of declaring the five-to-one majority decisive.
Use the project/family identifier to refer to the evolving lineage.
Bind the earlier result to exact version 4.1, preferably with its immutable digest/commit.
Label 'latest' as a moving alias now resolving to 4.2. Re-running on 4.2 is a new experiment, not exact reproduction of the 4.1 result.
Keep SEND_MESSAGE as the caller's abstract intent.
Provide environment handlers: FAIL_FAST, VERIFY_NON_DELIVERY_THEN_RETRY_ONCE, and SIMULATE_RECORD_ONLY.
The retrying handler must verify non-delivery or use an idempotency/effect identity before replay. The simulation handler records the requested effect but never marks external delivery as completed.
Changing handlers should not require rewriting the caller's business intent.
Define the target as structural old-API call nodes with the expected callee/signature shape, not raw token occurrences.
Exclude comments, strings, unrelated identifiers, and compatibility shims unless a separate rule explicitly covers them.
For every edit, persist the matched rule/location as its witness.
Run targeted tests/static checks and inspect the diff after transformation.
Create H1 and H2 as separate unresolved branches with their evidence and proposed remediations.
Simulate each remediation against its branch without changing protected production state.
Record the proposed change separately from any materialized effect.
Gather discriminating evidence, then merge/select or discard a branch only when that evidence justifies the collapse.
Encode the rule that analysis may read deployment state but cannot deploy/merge as a machine-checkable capability/target-authority boundary.
Exploration may surface an advisory violation, but the protected integration/deployment gate must hard-fail the forbidden call.
Refresh current policy/configuration before the gate check when stale state could create a false result.
Technical possession of a deploy-capable credential does not grant authorization.
First declare whether exact reconstruction is part of the compact representation's contract.
If exact, test original -> compact -> restored across defaults, ordering, empty values, unknown fields, and boundary cases, and fail on any undeclared loss.
If canonicalization/loss is intentional, enumerate the information allowed to disappear and do not claim byte- or structure-exact reconstruction.
